book.title: Tahorot

1.text: Said Rabbi Shimon: For what reason did they say, "food that is defiled by a father of impurity, and that is defiled by a secondary source of impurity join together" (Mishnah Tahorot 1:5). Because it it is possible for third-degree impurity to be made into second-degree impurity, and it is possible for second-degree impurity to be made into first-degree impurity. And for what reason did they say, "a sheretz and an animal carcass and a corpse do not join together"*note that unlike the previous citation, this statement does not appear our Mishnah? Because a sheretz cannot be made into an animal carcass, and an animal carcass cannot be made into corpse.
A piece of dough that possessed third-degree impurity and [other pieces] stuck to all of them possess third-degree impurity as to holy objects.

3.text: A child that was holding onto the hand of his father or that was riding on his father's shoulders: [When there is] a doubt regarding his [purity status], he is deemed impure, because his father is inquired of on his behalf. A deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor: [When there is] a doubt regarding their [purity status], they are deemed pure, because they do not have the mental capacity for inquiry. Said Rabbi Shimon: In regard to this [halacha], the logic is deficient.

An infant that is found standing next to a block of hardened dough*see Jastrow (כופת), or next to a jar of liquid, Rabbi Meir renders it pure and the Sages render it impure, for the nature of a child is to slap [his hand at the dough or the jar] (Mishnah Tahorot 3:7). Rabbi Yosei says, if he could reach out his hand and touch it, it is impure, and if not, it is pure. Furthermore, Rabbi Yosei says, [if the infant] is found far from the started dough*עיסה (an earlier stage in the doughmaking process than "hardened (or risen) dough" (בצק)), even though the hardened dough is in his hand, it is pure, for I could say, another [person] took [the hardened dough] and gave it to him, but if he said, "It is clear to me that no one came here*שלא בא אדם לכאן (MS Vienna; GR"A)," it is impure. Rabbi Ilai said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov*not "Rabbi Eliezer ben Yosei" (GR"A), in regards to a dog, behold, it is pure, for he can say, liquid is always to be found (i.e., is readily accessible), but food is not always to be found.

6.text: Regarding animal carcasses [animals not properly slaughtered] and properly slaughtered animals in a city, we follow the majority. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: Even if [only] one carcass is sold in the city, any [meat] found in the city is [presumed to be] from a carcass, because carcasses are commonly found. Regarding pure and impure blood in a house, we follow the majority. An incident occurred where blood was found on loaves of terumah [priestly offering], and the incident came before the Sages, and they declared them pure, for it was nothing other than the blood of live creeping creatures."

Nine creeping creatures [which are impure] and one frog [which is pure] are in the public domain, and a person touched one of them and does not know which of them he touched – his [status in this case of] doubt is pure. If one of them separated into the private domain, his doubt is impure. [If it separated] into the public domain, his doubt is pure. And regarding what is found [there], we follow the majority. Nine frogs and one creeping creature are in the private domain, and he touched one of them and does not know which of them he touched – his doubt is impure. If one of them separated into the private domain, his doubt is impure. [If it separated] into the public domain, his doubt is pure. And regarding what is found [there], follow the majority. An impure loaf that became mixed with nine pure loaves, and five people ate the first five, and afterwards five people ate the last five, and one of them became impure and does not know which of them it was – the first ones are impure, as they have nothing to attribute it to [to assume purity], and the last ones are pure. This is the general rule: a person against a person, pure items against pure items, a person against pure items, and pure items against a person – these serve as proofs. If the first ones were eaten, became impure, or were lost before the second ones were handled, they are pure. Once the second ones are handled, the second ones are suspended.

[Regarding] two paths, one impure and one pure, and he walked on one of them and prepared pure items, [and then walked] on the second and prepared [pure items] – they must be burned. [If he walked] on the first and did not prepare [pure items], and [then walked] on the second and prepared [pure items] – they must be burned. [If he walked] on the first and on the second, and prepared [pure items], both these and those remain resting [suspended in doubt]; the first ones are pure, and the second ones must be burned."
